Macau Casino Revenue Falls for a Fourth Straight Month

Published October 2, 2026 · 3 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Macau's casinos generated gross gaming revenue of MOP 18.06 billion ($2.23 billion) in September, down 1.2% from the same month in 2025, according to figures reported by Macau's Gaming Inspection and Coordination Bureau. It's the fourth consecutive month of year-over-year decline for the world's largest gambling hub, and the lowest single-month total of 2026, slipping below June's previous low of MOP 18.52 billion ($2.29 billion).

A sharp turn from earlier in the year

The slowdown marks a reversal from how 2026 started. Macau's gaming revenue was up 10.9% year-over-year from January through May, but has now declined for four straight months as momentum among premium and high-roller gamblers has softened. Going into September, some analyst forecasts had called for as much as 12% year-over-year growth; as floor checks through the month showed sluggish table play, brokerages scaled those projections back to marginal growth, and the final figure still missed the revised, lowered consensus. Weaker-than-expected premium mass table drop was cited as the main driver of the shortfall.

Despite the recent slide, Macau's revenue is still running ahead on a year-to-date basis: through the first three quarters of 2026, gross gaming revenue totaled MOP 187.11 billion ($23.15 billion), about 3.2% higher than the same period in 2025. Whether the fourth quarter can hold that gain is now an open question.

A tough comparison ahead, with a holiday tailwind

October brings its own complication: Macau posted MOP 24.08 billion ($2.98 billion) in casino win in October 2025, a high bar for this year's figure to clear. Working in the market's favor is Golden Week, the Oct. 1-7 holiday marking the founding of the People's Republic of China, which typically brings a surge of visitors from mainland China. Local tourism authorities are projecting average daily visitor arrivals of 120,000 during the holiday stretch.

Why it matters

Macau's monthly figures are closely watched well beyond Asia, since they're a direct read on the health of casino operators with major Macau exposure alongside their US operations, including Las Vegas Sands, Wynn Resorts, and MGM Resorts. A soft Macau print can weigh on how Wall Street views those companies' combined global casino businesses even when their US properties are performing well, and sustained weakness in premium play is a trend US-based casino watchers tend to track as an early signal of how discretionary, high-end gambling spending is holding up more broadly.
